name: Quartz
chronometers: Ti-in-quartz thermometry; OSL/ESR dating; cosmogenic nuclides

matrix.title: Prism length × rhombohedron balance
matrix.subtitle: Rows lengthen the m{101̄0} prism, from the bipyramid of volcanic quartz to needles. Columns balance the two rhombohedra r and z, and the last column adds the trigonal faces s and x that reveal a right-handed crystal.
matrix.note: Eight interfacial angles match Dana (1892) to within 0.02°, for example m∧r = 38.22° against 38°13′. Point group 32 has no mirrors or inversion, so r and z are different forms, s is a trigonal bipyramid and x a trigonal trapezohedron. Handedness follows Dana's morphological convention; the link to the P3₁21 or P3₂21 label is notoriously confusing (Donnay & Le Page 1978), so no space-group label is attached to the right-handed crystals. On real crystals r and z are told apart by etching; here r is simply the larger rhombohedron. Dauphiné and Brazil twins and tapering 'Tessin' habits are not modelled.

about:
Quartz looks hexagonal but is trigonal, with point group 32. The six terminal faces are really two different rhombohedra, r and z. They are often unequal, so alternate termination faces differ in size. The small s and x faces appear only on one side of each prism face and reveal whether a crystal is left- or right-handed.

Habit tracks conditions. Quartz phenocrysts in rhyolites and porphyries are prismless bipyramids, often paramorphs after high-temperature β-quartz (Hosaka et al. 1995). Vein and Alpine-fissure quartz is prismatic with sector-zoned r, z and m faces (Jourdan et al. 2009). Ti-in-quartz thermometry (TitaniQ) can depend on which growth sector a spot hits.

habits.name: Prismatic
habits.text: m prism with r and z terminations, r usually larger (row P2, column b).

habits.name: Bipyramidal
habits.text: No prism, r ≈ z: volcanic quartz grown as β-quartz (row B).

habits.name: Pseudocubic
habits.text: r alone forms a near-cubic rhombohedron, r∧r′ = 85°46′ (row B, column d).

habits.name: Right-handed
habits.text: Small s and x faces at alternate corners of the prism (column R).
